text:
maria_cs: FYI — AcmeCo goes live Mon 09:00 PST. They reported higher-than-expected token spend and a few latency spikes during pilot. They've signaled this could affect renewal unless we show quick mitigations. Need a concise customer-facing checklist (single page) + a short ops fallback plan we can ship to them. Can we draft here and pick an owner? @omar_cs @liam_pm :wave:

omar_cs: I can draft it now. High level: keep it super short — 3 sections: client caching, request batching, streaming & graceful degradation. Each section: one-sentence why + one concrete action + example config/snippet.

liam_pm: Agree. Customers want actionable steps. Also add a tiny "If things go sideways" flow (who to call, quick toggles).

sam_sre: From infra side, fallback plan should be: 1) route to lighter model variant, 2) enable token-level rate limit (soft queue), 3) flip on server-side prefix cache. We can prepare a canary route and a toggle in the Console.

maria_cs: Nice. Omar — paste your quick checklist draft here and I'll iterate for customer tone. I'll also set a 30-min sync with Acme CS lead after we have it.

omar_cs: Draft below — short and customer-facing. Tell me what to simplify.

omar_cs: "Acme Customer Checklist — Fast wins to reduce cost & latency"
- "Client caching — why: avoid repeated context tokens for similar inputs. Action: add a short-lifespan cache keyed by (user_id + prompt_hash). Example header to use when hitting Redwood API:"
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>
X-Client-Cache-Key: user_{{user_id}}:prompt_{{hash}}
Cache-Control: max-age=60
```
- "Batching requests — why: grouping small requests reduces per-token overhead. Action: backend should aggregate user prompts into micro-batches (<=200ms hold window). Example SDK options:"
```json
{"batch_max_size":8, "batch_hold_ms":50, "max_batch_tokens":2048}
```
- "Streaming & graceful degrade — why: streaming improves perceived latency; degrade reduces cost during spikes. Action: enable streaming for long responses and configure a model-fallback policy. Example policy snippet (pseudocode):"
```
if median_response_time > 300ms:
  route_to: "llama-7b-128q"
  enable_streaming: false  # fall back to synchronous short-mode with smaller model
else:
  use_primary_model
```
- "Ops fallback quick steps (customer-facing):"
  1) Toggle to reduced concurrency in Console (Path: Settings > Routes > AcmeRoute).
  2) Request CS to enable "Economy Mode" for your account (we'll route to a cheaper variant).
  3) Contact support with subject "AcmeCo — URGENT latency" and include last 15 min of request IDs.

omar_cs: That is intentionally terse — should fit a one-page email.

liam_pm: Language looks good. For the email out to the customer, change any internal path references to a short explanation ("Console > Routes" is fine). Also add one line: "We will run a brief calibration window with you: 30 min at low concurrency to validate improvements."

maria_cs: I'll shorten and send. Who owns the deploy/runbook to make the toggles painless? @sam_sre? :point_up:

sam_sre: I'll own runbook steps for toggles and the canary route. Quick notes for the runbook (ops side, internal):
- Pre-check: capture 3 example request IDs from the client and a recent failing time window.
- Create canary: route "acme-lowcost" pointing to smaller variant, set up traffic-split 95/5 initially.
- For immediate relief: flip route to 100% to cheaper variant, enable prefix cache, and temporarily reduce per-customer concurrency to 5.
- Rollback: revert route and remove reduced concurrency.

sam_sre: I'll also add a Console template toggle we can reuse for future renewal-risk clients.

maria_cs: Awesome. Final ask: Omar, can you post a one-paragraph cover note we can paste in the customer email (friendly tone, bullet link to checklist)? I'll then schedule the calibration call.

omar_cs: Cover note draft:
"Hi Team — we looked into your pilot traffic and prepared three quick changes that typically reduce cost and improve latency: client-side caching, batching at the backend, and a short streaming/degrade policy. Below is a one-page checklist with steps your engineers can do today and a short ops fallback we can flip for you if you hit a spike. We're ready to run a 30-minute calibration window with you at a time that works. — Omar, CS"

liam_pm: :thumbsup: Looks good. Maria, ping when it's sent and we'll monitor metrics. I'll add a tiny dashboard for the calibration window (p99, tokens/min, errors).

deploy-bot: Canary deploy "acme-lowcost" completed for route acme-route — version v2026-03-20_2205 — status: success

maria_cs: Sending in 10. Adding calendar invite for calibration. Assigning owners: Omar = customer message + checklist send; Sam = runbook + toggles; Liam = dashboard; Maria = calendar + client coordination. Closing thread once sent. :white_check_mark:
